Subject: Cross-region safeguard escalation & activation playbook — APAC pin + transient rollback

Hi Anika / Medicov security team —

Following our onboarding call last week, we sketched an activation + rollback playbook for the APAC region-pin you requested. The attached draft outlines:
- Activation steps for APAC subprocessor handshake (hours 0–8)
- Telemetry assertions we require pre- and post-activation (token-level logs, egress counts, KMS access events)
- A short rollback procedure if transient cross-region routing appears (48h window)

Two asks to validate from your side before we lock the schedule:
1) Can Medicov approve the proposed 72-hour canary window (we run 1% traffic -> 25% -> ramp) and the system-level alerts that will trigger automatic rollback?
2) Confirm whether you require KMS split-keys or just HSM-backed keys — the playbook assumes HSM only.

We expect to run the first canary on Oct 12 (APAC morning). If you need a different date, flag now — ops needs 72 hours to stage the subprocessor roster.

Attaching: medicov-safeguard-playbook-v1.pdf and a draft roster.

Thanks —

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear draft. A few clarifying questions from our security and legal team:

1) Rollback triggers — we need the exact telemetry threshold that causes an automatic rollback. Is it a token egress delta > 5% outside APAC for a 15-minute window, or do you use a different metric?
2) Subprocessor roster — please confirm whether the APAC edge cache will ever perform short-term reprocessing in the US for analytics. Medicov’s policy requires zero analytics reprocessing outside APAC during the 72h canary.
3) Key handling — we prefer split-keys (customer hold + Redwood HSM) for the first activation. Is that achievable for the APAC pilot?

Finally, we need an escalation contact — someone on call who can approve an immediate stop/rollback outside normal hours. Please provide a 24/7 escalation list.

Best,
Anika Rao

Hi Anika —

Quick answers from ops/infra (I’ve attached the activation roster CSV with node locations):

1) Rollback metric: we will use a composite rule — automatic rollback is triggered if BOTH conditions occur within a rolling 15-minute window:
   - >=5% of requests for the canary cohort observed egressing to non-APAC endpoints; AND
   - token-level KMS events show at least one re-encryption/access outside APAC.
   This composite reduces false positives. Manual rollback can be triggered immediately by the escalation list below.

2) Analytics reprocessing: the APAC edge cache is configured for request-scoped KV caching only. Under the canary we will NOT perform batch analytics reprocessing outside APAC. We will also block automatic telemetry exports to US analytics queues for the canary cohort. Ops tested this in staging — results attached.

3) Split-keys: we can support a split-key flow for the pilot. Requirements: Medicov must provide the customer-controlled key share in a KMS importable format 48 hours before activation. We will provide a simple HSM+import guide.

Escalation list (24/7):
- Jordan Blake (On-call Infra Lead) — jordan.blake@redwood.com — +1 415-555-0182
- David Kim (Product Security) — david.kim@redwood.com — +1 650-555-0239

Operational notes:
- Canary schedule: Oct 12 02:00 UTC start (APAC morning). 1% -> 10% -> 25% over 72 hours if no rollback.
- Pre-activation checklist: roster uploaded, canary cohort pinned, KMS split-key imported, telemetry gates green.

Attaching: apac-subprocessor-activation-roster.csv, staging-telemetry-sample.txt

—Marissa

Anika —

Thanks for the thorough review. To make the operational runbook concrete, here are the escalation and rollback instructions we will follow (and will encode in automations):

1) Monitoring + automated rollback (primary):
   - Metric feed: per-request region tag + egress destination tag + KMS access log.
   - Composite rule (as Marissa described). If rule trips, system will automatically pause the canary routing and divert remaining canary traffic to the pre-approved EU fallback model (no US egress).

2) Manual emergency stop (human-in-the-loop):
   - Who can stop: Jordan Blake (infra lead), David Kim (product security), Anika Rao (Medicov SPM) or Medicov CISO. Any one of the four can initiate.
   - How to stop: Slack #redwood-ops-esc and press-button in Console -> Canary -> Abort. The abort will preserve in-flight requests and produce a signed audit event for your legal team.

3) Rollback verification checklist (post-stop):
   - Confirm canary cohort diverted to EU fallback (audit event + trace ids)
   - Confirm no telemetry export to US analytics (audit)
   - Export KMS access events for the canary cohort window (signed bundle)

4) Post-incident remediation window:
   - If rollback is due to transient misrouting, we can attempt a re-run after a 24h investigation and fix. Any re-run requires signed approval from Medicov security.

I’ll add these steps to the playbook PDF and upload an updated version by EOD.
